title: Eid al-Adha: the day
hookLine: the prayer, the sacrifice, the sharing, the visits

lines: THEIR FLESH AND BLOOD REACH NOT ALLAH.
cards: "Their flesh and their blood reach not Allah, but the devotion from you reacheth Him." A line from Surah al-Hajj, in Pickthall's translation, and a strange thing to say on the morning of a sacrifice. The animal is real.
The knife is real. The meat will be cooked and eaten by nightfall. And the verse says none of that is what reaches Allah.
Something else does. Today, Eid al-Adha, the feast of the sacrifice, and a morning with an order to it.

teach.h: FIRST THE PRAYER, THEN THE SACRIFICE.
teach.b: First, the prayer. Al-Bara' reports in al-Bukhari that the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, said, in paraphrase: the first thing we do on this day of ours is pray, then go back and sacrifice.
The sacrifice comes after the prayer, not before. Second, the sacrifice. The Qur'an tells of Ibrahim, ready to give up his son, and then: "Then We ransomed him with a tremendous victim."

teach.h: AN ANIMAL WHERE THE SON STOOD.
teach.b: The animal stands where the son stood. Families who can afford it offer a sheep, a goat, a cow or a share in a camel, or pay for one to be offered on their behalf. Third, where the meat goes.

The same surah says of the animals: "eat thereof and feed the beggar and the suppliant." Eat, and feed. Some scholars recommend dividing it: some for the household, some for relatives and friends, some for those in need.
The feast is not kept whole. Fourth, the visits.
The rest of the day, and the days after, people go from house to house, carry plates to neighbors, sit with the old aunt they don't see enough. Prayer, then the knife, then the plate, then the door.
The devotion is what reaches Allah. The meat goes the other way, out across the street, into other people's kitchens.

how: On Eid al-Adha, Muslims go to the Eid prayer, and afterward those who can afford it offer an animal in sacrifice, or pay for one to be offered, and share its meat with family, friends and people in need; the day is also for visiting relatives and neighbors.

o: the feast of the sacrifice, during the hajj
the night the Qur'an was first revealed
a welcome feast for pilgrims coming home

p: first the prayer, then the sacrifice
the devotion, not flesh or blood

s: on Eid al-Adha the sacrifice comes before the prayer
al-Bara' reports the Prophet saying the first thing is to pray, then go back and sacrifice.
the Qur'an says the flesh and blood of the sacrifice reach Allah
"Their flesh and their blood reach not Allah, but the devotion from you reacheth Him."
the Qur'an tells those who sacrifice to eat and to feed others
"eat thereof and feed the beggar and the suppliant."

games.q: it's the morning of Eid al-Adha. the animal is ready, the prayer is soon. what comes first?
o: the sacrifice, so the meat is ready.
games.why: al-Bara' reports it: the first thing we do on this day is pray, then go back and sacrifice.

practice: Think of what you'll eat today or later this week, and picture one plate of it going out the door instead of onto your table. Who gets it: a neighbor you only wave at, a friend having a hard month, someone living alone?
If you pray, remember the verse, the devotion is what reaches Him; if not, just hold the picture of the plate in someone else's hands.

wordCard.voice: Eid al-Adha. The feast of the sacrifice at the height of the hajj: prayer first, then the sacrifice, then the meat shared out, then the visits. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the name of the feast of the sacrifice.

carryVoice: Your line: share the feast. Eat, and feed. I'll be here tomorrow.
